queries: Hallucination of Multimodal Large Language Models: A Survey arXiv 2024

sources_considered.why: OpenAI's own system card for GPT-4V (September 2023) reports that the model hallucinated.
HallusionBench (CVPR 2024; version dated March 2024) tested GPT-4V, Gemini Pro Vision and Claude 3 and found heavy hallucination failures.
Survey posted two weeks after the post. It describes multimodal LLM hallucination as a frequent and unsolved problem. Used as context only, because it was published after the target period ends.

receipt.public_excerpt:
Additionally, the model was prone to hallucinations and sometimes could
make factual errors in an authoritative tone.

evidence_items.explanation: The developer of GPT-4V, the main model that added vision to an LLM, reports that it was still prone to hallucinations.

receipt.public_excerpt: we benchmarked 15 different models, highlighting a 31.42% question-pair accuracy achieved by the state-of-the-art GPT-4V. Notably, all other evaluated models achieve accuracy below 16%.

evidence_items.explanation: A benchmark of leading vision-language models, including GPT-4V, Gemini Pro Vision and Claude 3, found low accuracy and documented hallucination failure modes weeks before the post.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv (Bai et al., NUS Show Lab / AWS)

receipt.public_excerpt: MLLMs often generate outputs that are inconsistent with the visual content, a challenge known as hallucination, which poses substantial obstacles to their practical deployment

evidence_items.explanation: A research survey posted shortly after the post describes multimodal LLM hallucination as frequent and an obstacle to deployment. This agrees with the claim, but it falls outside the target period, so it is context only.

unresolved_gaps: The GPT-4V system card notes that hallucinations were reduced during the Be My Eyes beta. This shows progress, not a solution, and it does not contradict the claim.
